claim.why_it_matters: FACTORIAL function and FACTORY clause are merged on one line, and the whole F block is flattened to one indent level so sub-entries (METHOD-ID paragraph, USAGE clause, EVALUATE statement, FILE-CONTROL paragraph ...) are indistinguishable from top-level entries.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 867 (folio 845, right column, F section) shows 'FACTORIAL function 600' and 'FACTORY clause' on separate lines, with sub-entries indented under their heads: METHOD-ID paragraph 181 under FACTORY clause; Life cycle for 166 under Factory object; USAGE clause 361 under FACTORY phrase; EVALUATE statement 441 and SET statement, condition setting 516 under FALSE phrase; FILE-CONTROL paragraph 212 and RECORD DELIMITER clause 225 under Feature-name. The rest of the page in page-867.md marks sub-entries with ' '. In the F block (lines 97-117) the first two entries are joined as 'FACTORIAL function 600 FACTORY clause', and every later entry has the same three-space indent with no ' '. That loses the parent/child structure, so a sub-entry such as 'USAGE clause 361' or 'EVALUATE statement 441' reads as a top-level index entry. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The defect is structural index content, not page furniture, and it is not normative.
verdict.corrected_description: In the F block, the transcription joins 'FACTORIAL function 600' and 'FACTORY clause' into one line. It also flattens every following entry to the same plain three-space indent, dropping the ' ' sub-entry markers used on the rest of the page. As a result, the children METHOD-ID paragraph, Life cycle for, USAGE clause, EVALUATE statement, SET statement (condition setting), FILE-CONTROL paragraph and RECORD DELIMITER clause can no longer be told apart from top-level entries.
